chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Ablution is a limit from the limits of Allah, so that Allah may know who obeys Him and who disobeys Him, and indeed the believer is not polluted by anything; rather, the like of oil suffices for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of wudu and how is a believer's purity defined in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) defines wudu as a specific divine boundary (hadd) designed to test obedience, emphasizing that for a believer, ritual purity is not compromised by external impurities. He clarifies that even minor substances like oil do not render the body impure, highlighting the Shia principle of the inherent purity of the believer's body unless explicitly defined otherwise. This underscores the theological view that wudu is an act of worship and submission rather than merely a mechanical cleansing process.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘But rather, the Ablution (Wudhu) is a Limit from the Limits of Allahazwj in order to Allahazwj to Know the one who obeys Himazwj and the one who disobeys Himazwj, and that the Believer cannot be polluted by anything. But rather, he would be suffice from the likes of the oil (from the water)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Wudu’ is one of the boundaries Allah has established so that He finds out who obeys or disobeys Him. The believing people do not allow it (their body) to remain unclean. It is sufficient to use a small amount of water like rubbing oil on one’s body.’”
